function.name: run_shell
function.description: Run a shell command in the workspace and return its exit code, stdout and stderr. Use this to install dependencies, build, run tests, or start the setup. Commands run in a sandbox: the workspace is writable, the home directory is empty, secret files (.env*, private keys, credentials) are hidden, .git and the tool's own code are read-only, and there is NO network unless you set needs_network. With it, the command reaches the internet only by HTTP(S) through a proxy that is already set in HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY, and only package registries (PyPI, npm, crates.io, Go, GitHub, Hugging Face), hosts written in the command and hosts the user allowed; other hosts are blocked and listed in the result. No ssh, ping or UDP. Background processes end when the command ends; /tmp is kept for the rest of this chat. To read a web page use fetch_url if you have it, not curl. Destructive or risky commands are shown to the user, who may decline.

command.description: The command line to run, e.g. 'python -m pytest'.
